text:
Happy Sunday, and you got the extra hour of sleep. We're starting clear and frosty at 30 this morning, so the windshield may need a scrape. High pressure is sliding offshore, and that's turning the wind around to the south, so the day warms up nicely. Expect plenty of sunshine and a high near 57, with a light breeze you'll barely notice. The sun sets at 4:41 now, so get your walk or ride in earlier than you think you need to. Tonight is milder, with a low around 40.

Monday is dry and warmer, near 62, and a couple of the models push it into the mid 60s. Tuesday is the one to watch: more clouds than sun, and a shower is possible, though the models disagree and the amounts look tiny. I'd keep the umbrella in the car, not in your hand. Wednesday is the warm one, near 70, but the south wind turns gusty, 15 to 25 mph with a few gusts near 30. Rain looks likely to settle in by Thursday.

week.blurb: Sunny and mild for November, a high near 57 after a frosty start, so it's a good day to get outside.
Mostly sunny and a touch warmer, low 60s, though some models push toward the mid 60s.
Showers become possible after 1, mostly light, but some models run wetter, so keep an umbrella handy with a high near 61.
The warmest day of the week, partly sunny and dry, with a high near 68.
Clouds thicken with a chance of rain from the morning on, then rain becomes likely after dark, high near 65.
Mostly cloudy with a high near 61 and a decent chance of rain at times, turning cooler by evening.
Looks like more clouds and a chance of showers, with a cooler high near 55 if the pattern holds.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-11-01T06:56:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Temperatures becoming warmer heading into November.
  2. A cold front will move through the Northeast late this week bringing breezes and periods of rain possibly Thursday through the weekend.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 152 AM EST Sunday... Rainfall prospects for Tuesday are somewhat higher, and temperatures for Wednesday have been trended upwards to near record warmth in the St. Lawrence Valley.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Little in the manner of impactful weather is expected over the next several days. High pressure will move offshore, and that will allow warm air to gradually filter into the region under steady south to southwest flow. This will bring 50s today, and then 60s tomorrow. It'll still be on the dry side, but winds will generally be lighter where the lowest humidity values will be. Nighttime temperatures will also trend warmer, with only cooler hollows of sheltered valleys east of any mountain slopes below freezing tonight. There's still a tilted mid to upper level ridge that will be positioned to our west through about Tuesday. As it begins to translate eastwards, depending on the positioning of an upper vort, the surge of warm, moist advection could become collocated with marginal synoptic forcing. This would result in an area of clouds and light rain, mainly along the international border Tuesday into Tuesday night. Not every model scenario depicts rain, and so PoPs are mainly at or below 50 percent at this time. Once the upper ridge is offshore, temperatures will climb into the mid 60s to lower 70s for Wednesday in response to somewhat tighter pressure gradients as a surface low tracks over far northern Quebec Province. A few daily record highs may be in striking distance. Ushering in the warmth will be south winds gusting around 15-25 mph with localized observations around 30 mph, especially in the broader valleys. KEY MESSAGE 2: Model consensus favors a full meridional trough ejecting out of the Plains Wednesday night with a cold frontal passage through the Northeast between Thursday and Friday. Timing spread has narrowed a little, but model discrepancies remain on how fast the high pressure shifts eastward, the timing of the front itself, and the strength of frontal dynamics. Some models are stalling the boundary in the vicinity of Vermont streaming ample moisture across the region while others are more progressive with flow resulting in more distinct rounds of rainfall. While the details are sparse, most guidance shares that there is a good shot at an extended period of rain chances which the trailing upper low becoming at least partially cut off. This would promote lingering shower chances through the weekend potentially into early next week. The details that are more predictable are continued warm temperatures under southerly flow Thursday with some southerly breezes ongoing as well. Beyond Thursday, temperatures are favored to cool back towards seasonal averages with coldest air locked well north of the region.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - A reminder to turn your clocks back 1 hour before bedtime tonight. We’re back to Standard Time at 2 AM on Sunday. After a chilly but fair Halloween, Sunday will be mostly sunny and pleasantly warmer with highs in the 50s to around 60 degrees...not a bad way to start November and the second half of fall. Monday will be dry and even warmer with highs in the mid-50s to low 60s. The week will continue to be dry before the chance for rain increases late in the week. Election Day may have an isolated shower north, otherwise it will be mostly cloudy with highs in the 50s, though a few low 60s are possible. The warmest day will be Wednesday with plenty of sunshine and highs in the 60s. A few spots may even hit 70 degrees. It will be breezy, so we’ll have to keep an eye on the fire danger. The risk is currently high in parts of the region, but it’s not expected to reach red flag status. We’ll keep an eye on it. A storm system will bring some needed rain late in the week and possibly into next weekend, though models differ with the track and duration. As of now, Thursday is expected to be mostly cloudy with showers likely. Friday and Saturday are a bit more uncertain, but the chance for showers may continue. High temperatures those days will be in the 50s with lows in the 40s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-31T22:37:00Z — same caveat): Brighter and warmer Sunday as a south wind takes over — Tonight will feature a mostly clear sky, and it turns colder. Lows reach the 20s to around 30 for most. A few outlying towns may dip back to the teens. Sunday turns milder, with highs closer to 60°, as a light south breeze develops. High pressure brings a mostly sunny sky through the day. Most of next week looks mild for early November, with highs pushing past 60 several days in a row. Monday will have sun, but Tuesday looks to bring more clouds than sun. A few showers may pass by on Tuesday with a warm front. Highs will be in the 60s both days, however. Wednesday looks to be the warmest and brightest day. Highs will be near 70, with a gusty south breeze and partly sunny skies. Clouds thicken up Thursday, followed by a chance for more widespread rain overnight into Friday, as an area of low pressure approaches from the southwest.
